messages:
Zoe: sec-bot flagged a debug archive in s3://redwood-backups/dev/2026-03-16.tar.gz that contains a file with what looks like an API key. I haven't touched prod systems yet. What immediate steps should I take?

Jess: which key string? can you paste the surrounding line (redact 4+ chars) and the object path?

Zoe: path above. snippet shows `api_key=sk-prod-1a2b3c4d5e` (i redacted middle). archive is in a private bucket (not public). sec-bot said it found a pattern.

Kyle: treat as compromised until proven otherwise. Revoke/rotate asap if it's a prod key. Also search usage in the last 30m/24h to see if there's any traffic. If it's encrypted with KMS and only stored as ciphertext, less urgent, but from your snippet it looks plaintext.

Matt: +1. If it's a service account token (CI), revoke the token and create a replacement with least privilege. If it's a customer-facing key, follow customer disclosure policy. For now: 1) suspend the key 2) rotate/create replacement 3) run a one-off audit for usage 4) delete artifact and add a preventive step. Playbook: https://redwood.internal/security/rotations/playbook (internal).

Jess: quick commands I used locally to confirm: ```bash
# list and inspect file from tar without extracting
tar -tzf 2026-03-16.tar.gz | grep debug || true
tar -xOf 2026-03-16.tar.gz path/to/file | sed -n '1,120p' | grep -E 'sk-[A-Za-z0-9]+'
```
If you need to search S3 for other copies: `aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-backups --query "Contents[?contains(Key, '2026-03')].Key"` then `aws s3 cp s3://... - | tar -xzO | grep -i sk-`

sec-bot: automated alert: secret_pattern_match=sk-*, bucket=redwood-backups, object=dev/2026-03-16.tar.gz, risk=high :rotating_light: (this is an automated flag, verify with humans).

Zoe: who has authority to rotate this key? I'm not set up to rotate prod service keys.

Kyle: infra leads + sec oncall can rotate. If the key is owned by a service team, they should rotate; infra can assist. If you're unsure, tag @infra-oncall and @sec-oncall. If immediate vulnerability suspected, page.

Matt: small tolerance: if you confirm plaintext prod key, rotate immediately and update deployments to use new key via vault. Steps: 1) create new secret in Vault/KMS-wrapped store 2) update k8s secret or env var in CI 3) trigger canary deploy 4) expire old key after verification. I can do the Vault write if you assign.

Jess: i'll run a quick scan across backups for similar patterns and share findings. also will grep CloudWatch for any calls using that key id (if logs contain token fragments).

Zoe: ok assigning: Matt — please create vault entry and rotate the prod key. Jess — sweep backups & logs for occurrences. I'll remove the archive item and create a ticket referencing rotation playbook. tagging infra-oncall.

Matt: on it. I'll rotate and post new secret locations here when done.

Jess: found two more small archives containing the same pattern (dev/2026-02-27.tar.gz, dev/2026-01-10.tar.gz). Marked for deletion after rotation.

sec-bot: note: removed from watchlist: false. continue monitoring.

Matt: rotated key, updated Vault at secret/services/prod/api (rotated by matt), replaced env var in deployment config, triggered canary. Old key revoked via IAM. Deployed to canary cluster, no errors so far.

Zoe: archive objects deleted from backups bucket, tickets: SEC-1124 (rotation) and INFRA-783 (artifact cleanup). Jess, please follow up with a short postmortem on how debug archives are created with sensitive material and add a CI step to strip secrets before archiving.

Jess: will do a PR to add a linter/hook to strip env files and a CI check that fails if `sk-` tokens are present.

Zoe: thanks everyone, closing this thread after pending PR review. :lock:
